Definition: Treating poverty, smallness, or obscurity as proof of correctness. Being small or persecuted does not by itself make a claim true.
Example: Someone argues, 'This small unknown brand must be better — the big companies are corrupt.'
FaithDiscussionExample: Someone argues, 'That tiny persecuted group must have the truth — the big churches are compromised.'
HowToRespond: Apply one standard to all sizes: 'Smallness isn't proof either — let's examine the claims.'
